test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Kumar Mangalam Birla Committee was set up to look into which of the following areas of Indian economy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Corporate governance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kumar Mangalam Birla Committee (1999)

 
 
• It was constituted by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to recommend a code of corporate governance.
 
• The committee laid the foundation for the SEBI's code of corporate governance in India.
 
• Its recommendations led to the insertion of Clause 49 in the Listing Agreement, which prescribed mandatory and non-mandatory provisions for corporate governance for listed companies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Corporate Governance

 
 
• It refers to the system by which companies are directed and controlled.
 
• It involves regulatory and market mechanisms, roles and relationships between a company’s management, its board, shareholders, and other stakeholders.
 
 
 
• Clause 49 of the Listing Agreement
 
 
• Introduced by SEBI in 2000 based on the recommendations of the Kumar Mangalam Birla Committee.
 
• It mandates specific corporate governance practices such as the composition of the board, the role of independent directors, and the establishment of audit committees.
 
 
 
• SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)
 
 
• It is the regulator for the securities market in India.
 
• SEBI’s primary function is to protect the interests of investors in securities and to promote the development of, and regulate, the securities market.
